full_judgment:
57. The GO Entry, which is the first information report in the legal sense, shows that the assailants were three unidentified youths. So, recognition of the assailants is very much doubtful. Complicity of the accused persons is an after-thought. Moreover, it is not the prosecution case that the deceased was senseless from being injured to till death and he was incapable to speak. So, presumption would be that he had capability to speak. But he did not disclose the names of the accused as his assailants. It raises doubt as to the truth of the prosecution case. 

 59. PWs 2, 8 and 20 did not mention the names of accused Khaja and Sohrab in their statements recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. They said that, they did not know their names at that time. It is not said how they could know their names subsequently. In the belated first information report also, the names of these two accused did not find place. It is not stated in first information report that PW 2 was chatting with the deceased at the material time and PW 2 with others shifted the deceased to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. It is also not mentioned in the first information report that PWs 8 and 20 shifted the deceased. Without any explanation Swapan and Jashim, two eye-witnesses cited in the charge sheet, were withheld. So, presumption would be that had they been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case. PW 2 did not disclose to PW 21 in the evening following the occurrence that he saw the occurrence and reccgnised the assailants. PWs 8 and 20 did not state in their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that PW 2 accompanied them at the time of shifting the deceased to the hospital. PW 2 contradicted PWs 6, 8 and 20 saying that PWs 8 and 20 were not in the vehicle by which the deceased was shifted to the hospital. PW 2, for the first time, disclosed about his presence at the scene and recognition of the accused persons to PW 21 one day after lodging first information report, when his statement was recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. PW 2 stated that 10/15 minutes after going to the hospital he returned to the park in' search of some important papers he had left there. He did not say where he left the papers and what was the papers. He said that returning to the park he could not find out his papers, but found out those later on. Next two days of occurrence he also visited the hospital. He was a witness of seizure of alamats on two different dates and in different places. Thus, PW 2 Sharif appears to be a very much interested witness.
